cloze.title: 原文选词填空
cloze.instruction: 从词库中选择合适的词填入空白，每词使用一次，保留原文词形。大小写不影响判分。

parts.text: This matters, because who we go to school with fundamentally shapes our experience of education and our

on life.

These inequalities in intakes between private and state schools have been invisible until now.

When students from deprived backgrounds are unevenly distributed between schools, attainment gaps – the difference in academic
between richer and poorer students – tend to be larger. The segregation of our schools by social class makes educational inequality worse. Less segregated, more

mixed schools would improve achievement for all – and especially for lower-attaining students.

Grammar schools, which ostensibly select students by academic ability, are disproportionately middle class. Research has found that once their

intake is accounted for, grammar schools are “no better or worse than the other schools in England”

Class segregation between schools is quite simply unfair. This is why there was support for the abolition of selective schooling in the 1960s, when

schools were introduced in all but a few parts of England. Phasing out grammar schools was popular because the class inequalities in opportunity and attainment they caused was obvious.

But this reform did not include private schools, a key

of educational inequality.

Concentrating advantage

More than any other school type, private schools concentrate wealth and advantage. Private schools educate barely any

students. In my research with colleagues, less than 3% of students in UK private schools were from the lowest social classes, compared to 16.7% in state schools and colleges.

We know that private schools are disproportionately attended by the highest

and the upper middle classes. Yet we know almost nothing about how private schools affect the sorting and segregation of social classes between schools.

In our paper, we looked at the extent to which the social class

of schools in local authority areas differs from the country as a whole. This allowed us to measure whether some areas had schools which were more segregated than others. Greater segregation meant that schools had more
distribution of working or middle class students relative to the national distribution.

reading.title: 主旨、理解与信息定位
reading.instruction: 阅读原文后回答 5 道选择题：1 道主旨、1 道内容理解、1 道段落细节、2 道信息定位。段落细节题以题干指定段落为准。

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarises the overall focus of this article?
options: Public libraries support communities in many ways and need resources to sustain that work.
A heavy burden of standardised testing does not necessarily lead to better learning.
Private schooling can reinforce class separation and wider social divisions.
A long-term study links public prekindergarten attendance to better later educational outcomes.
questions.explanation: 把标题与全文各段的中心内容连起来判断主旨，避免把同一主题下的其他话题当成本文重点。
questions.evidence: If you want to see how private schools in the UK can reinforce segregation between children of different social classes, the London Borough of Southwark provides a good example.
